summary: refuse a class claim that the source lacks
pull_request_body: A stage plan can build on a claim about an internal class that the class source does not hold, and every check accepts the plan. The change adds a rule to the `paths` gate of `check_proposal`: a design decision, a rejected alternative or a feasibility line that names an internal class in a code span gives another code span whose text the class holds at the staged commit. The stage job reads each class that a claim names with `git show`, and the replay reads the class source from the facts of its case.
why: The plan of #3350 says that `StagedTree` holds the file text of the staged commit, and `StagedTree.read` keeps the tracked paths only, so an implementation step would fail on a text that does not exist (#3407).
what_changes: Refuse a class claim that gives no quote of the class at the staged commit, in the `paths` gate of `src/devops_cli/roadmap/stage/stage_change.py`.
Read each class that a claim names at the staged commit in `src/devops_cli/roadmap/stage/stage_models.py`.
Pass the class sources to the gate in `src/devops_cli/roadmap/stage/stage.py`.
Hold the cases of the rule in `tests/roadmap/stage/test_roadmap_stage_class_claim.py`.
feasibility: `read_file` of `src/devops_cli/roadmap/stage/stage_paths.py` showed `listing = git(source, "ls-files", "-z", operation=operation)` in the `read` classmethod, so the tree keeps the tracked paths and reads no file text.
`class_claim_problems` of `src/devops_cli/roadmap/stage/stage_change.py` is the new rule of the `paths` gate, and it compares a quote with the class source that `class_sources` reads.
The stage job computes the class sources from the names that `claimed_classes` returns, beside the model fields, and gives them to `check_gates`.
The facts of a replay case hold the class source, so the replay reads no git and makes no network call.
existing_tool: The change extends `check_proposal` and reuses the `git show` reader and the standard library `ast`, so it adds no dependency and no second grammar of a class.

decisions.decision: `StagedTree` holds the file text of the staged commit.
decisions.reason: The plan builds on that reader, so the group adds no second read of the tree and no new field of the case.

decisions.decision: Run the class-claim rule in the `paths` gate of `check_proposal`, beside `model_problems`.
decisions.reason: The stage job and the replay run that gate, so one rule judges both, and the golden case records the defect under it.

decisions.decision: Take the source of the class with `ast` and compare a whitespace-squashed quote of at least three characters with the squashed class source.
decisions.reason: A plan line folds a multi-line quote to one line, and a two-character quote matches almost any source, so the rule keeps the bound of the citation rule.

decisions.decision: State a non-goal: the rule judges no class that `src/` does not define, and no plan text other than the decisions, the rejected alternatives and the feasibility lines.
decisions.reason: A class of the standard library is no internal class, and a What Changes item or a task names a class without making a design claim.

rejected.alternative: Reuse the model reader `_grep_class_paths` unchanged for the new reader.
rejected.evidence: `src/devops_cli/roadmap/stage/stage_models.py:131:args = ["grep", "-n", f"^class {name}(", sha, "--", "src/"]` matches only a definition line with a base, and the class of the issue declares none, so the reader would return no source for it.

rejected.alternative: Compare each quote with the working tree instead of the staged commit.
rejected.evidence: The citation rule reads the staged commit, and the plan is judged at that commit, so a working tree can hold other text.

rejected.alternative: Scan every plan text for a class name.
rejected.evidence: The issue names the decisions, the rejected alternatives and the feasibility lines, and a What Changes item or a task names a class without making a design claim about it.

rejected.alternative: Find a class in the source text with a regular expression.
rejected.evidence: A regex matches a comment, a string or a local name, and the model reader uses the standard library `ast` to find the classes of a module.

added.name: A class claim quotes the class at the staged commit
added.text: `check_proposal` SHALL return a problem when a design decision, a rejected alternative or a feasibility line names an internal class under `src/` and gives no code span whose text the class holds at the staged commit.

scenarios.name: False StagedTree claim
scenarios.when: A design decision names the class StagedTree and quotes no text of the class.
scenarios.then: The plan check returns the class-claim problem for that decision.

groups.title: Refuse a class claim that the staged source lacks
groups.test: `tests/roadmap/stage/test_roadmap_stage_class_claim.py` fails on the base for `class_claim_problems`: a decision that names `StagedTree` with no quote is refused, and a test builds the plan's own `StageProposal` and asserts that `content_problems` returns no problem
groups.implementation: add `claimed_classes` and `class_claim_problems` to `src/devops_cli/roadmap/stage/stage_change.py` and call the second in the `paths` gate of `check_proposal`, add `class_sources` to `src/devops_cli/roadmap/stage/stage_models.py`, compute the class sources in `src/devops_cli/roadmap/stage/stage.py`, add `stage_problem_class_claim` to `src/devops_cli/lang/en/messages.py`, and run `uv run devops roadmap eval stage --replay` with the score before and after the change
